newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Basis fall temporarily halted.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Basis fall temporarily halted.

text.p: Basis bids for hard red winter wheat were steady Thursday as the recent slide came to a temporary halt amid a slowdown in farmer sales.

Dealers said the recent slide in prices had shut off producer sales. KCBT May HRW wheat futures closed at $4.14 a bushel Wednesday, well below this week's high of $4.32 set on Monday and basis levels at many locations have also fallen significantly over the last few days.
They noted that little rain appeared to have fallen in Kansas and Oklahoma this week despite forecasts for crop boosting showers.
"They (forecasters) keep saying it it going to rain tonight but it doesn't come," one Kansas dealer said, noting rain was again forecast for later Thursday.
Dealers said basis weakness was likely to resume soon as prices converge toward lower new crop levels. Sluggish demand also continued to weigh on basis bids, they added.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: K=KCBT May wheat futures. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
